# aibris v0.11.0

This release publishes protected-weight reclamation: guided review of every
tool's worktrees, `clean --strip` for regenerable subtrees inside protected
units, and optional volume-pressure cache selection. The next tag after
v0.10.0 is this feature/minor, not a v0.10.1 patch.

## Highlights

- Guided worktree review admits units from every agent tool. `--guide` still
  implies `--category worktree` but no longer implies `--tool codex`.
- `aibris clean --strip` reclaims regenerable subtrees (`node_modules`,
  venv, Flutter/Android/iOS build output) from worktrees that deletion
  protects, without deleting the unit or uncommitted work.
- `aibris scan` reports home-volume used percent, free bytes, and band
  (`ok` / `low` / `critical`). `clean --pressure` (or an automatic critical
  volume) may select official regenerable caches younger than `--age`.
- Registered worktree containers classify two-level
  `<owner>/<leaf>/<checkout>` members. Mixed markers still fail closed.
- `install.sh main` stamps `aibris version main-<shortsha>` and hints when
  the per-user zsh completion directory is not on `fpath`.

## Compatibility impact

**Breaking change** for the documented `--guide` default, plus **compatible
additions**.

`--guide` no longer implies `--tool codex`. Existing invocations that relied
on that implicit tool filter now review every tool's worktrees. The JSON
schema remains `schema_version: 1`. New optional `scan --json` field
`volume`, new `strippable_*` inventory fields, `--strip`, `--pressure`,
`--apfs-snapshots`, `--receipt-file`, `--agent-state-grace`, and the
`volume_pressure` reason code are additive. Existing documented fields,
defaults other than the `--guide` tool filter, and exit behavior are
unchanged.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.11.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.

## Upgrade and migration

If you previously ran guided review expecting only Codex worktrees, pass the
tool filter explicitly:

```bash
# v0.10.0 and earlier: --guide implied --tool codex
aibris clean --guide

# v0.11.0: same Codex-only review
aibris clean --guide --tool codex

# v0.11.0 default: every tool's worktrees
aibris clean --guide
```

`--guide` still implies `--category worktree`. `--tool` still narrows when
passed. Non-Codex units are never auto-recommended: they enter review as
`not-registered` unless a registered reader exists.

No migration is required for `scan --json` consumers. Ignore unknown optional
fields (`volume`, `strippable_bytes`, `strippable_paths`,
`total_strippable_bytes`). Stop on an unknown newer `schema_version`.

Volume pressure never deletes anything by itself. `--age` remains the floor
unless the home volume is critical or `--pressure` is set, and only
`build-cache` / `other-cache` relax. To restore the previous immediate
orphaned agent-state selection, pass `--agent-state-grace 0`.

```bash
aibris scan
aibris clean --dry-run
aibris clean --strip --dry-run
aibris clean --no-guide --pressure --dry-run --json
```

## Safety

- `plain-dir` and mixed-marker owners stay review-only and are never
  selected for deletion or strip.
- Strip refuses a unit that holds the current working directory, matching
  the deletion hard lock, and re-derives that barrier at mutation time.
- Automatic critical-volume mode relaxes only official caches on the home
  volume. Explicit `--pressure` applies to every official cache. Worktree,
  agent-state, and `--risky` gates are unchanged.
- `--apfs-snapshots` is opt-in and never part of default clean.
- Default `clean --json` output stays path-redacted. Volume `id` is a hashed
  device token, not a mount path.

## Windows status

Windows archives are **experimental**. The supported shape is the `amd64` /
`arm64` Windows zip archives cross-built by GoReleaser and listed in
`checksums.txt`. Native users verify the SHA-256 and place `aibris.exe` on
`PATH`; `install.sh` remains Unix-only. Volume inspection is omitted on
Windows. Pull-request CI builds and exercises the native executable
(`--version`, `--help`, isolated `scan --json`), home / cache isolation,
recorded-cwd volume safety, reparse-point cleanup protection, and hermetic
HOME fixture behavior on `windows-latest`. A Windows version matrix is not
published.

## Verification

Pre-tag verification passed `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and focused
`go test ./internal/volume ./internal/cleaner ./internal/adapter`. The
curated-release Windows-status validator must pass on this file. The tagged
release workflow publishes the six Darwin/Linux/Windows archives and
`checksums.txt`.

### Pre-tag dogfood

`install.sh main` installed `aibris version main-4283c7884f40` and printed
the zsh `fpath` hint without editing rc files.

A read-only real-home run used `aibris scan`, `aibris clean --no-guide
--dry-run --json`, `aibris clean --strip --dry-run`, and `aibris clean
--no-guide --pressure --dry-run --json`. No deletion occurred. Scan reported
236 items / 20.1 GB, home-volume band `low` at 90% used with 46.8 GB free,
and 2.5 GB strippable. The path-redacted default plan selected 4 physical
targets / 44.4 MB, with 85 worktree rows `worktree_requires_review` and 12
`active_worktree` protected. `--pressure` raised selected targets from 4 to
10 and labeled 6 rows `volume_pressure`; 3 rows stayed `minimum_age`. Strip
dry-run listed 5 candidates / 2.5 GB, including a registered two-level
checkout, and ended `[DRY-RUN] No files were removed.` JSON plans leaked
neither a home path nor `/Users/`.

An isolated temporary HOME verified mutation. Default dry-run selected one
4,096-byte `node_modules` target and skipped a 1-byte young official cache
as `minimum_age`. `--pressure --category=build-cache` selected that young
cache as `volume_pressure`. Classic execution
`clean --no-guide --json --force --category=node_modules` emitted a
`clean_receipt` schema version 1 with status `succeeded`, `requested: 1`,
`removed: 1`, and `freed_bytes: 4096`. Only the fixture target was deleted;
the young cache remained.

See [docs/DOGFOOD.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.11.0/docs/DOGFOOD.md)
for the sanitized record.
